cards.prose: Look at what the devil left off when he quoted this at the pinnacle. The promise is that the angels keep him *in all thy ways*, and a leap from the temple roof is nobody's way, it is a dare. Yahusha (Jesus) walks the ways of Yahuah (the LORD), and he will not stage a stunt to make the Father prove himself.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The psalm promises angels will keep him in all his ways, which the devil's quotation of it passes over.

cards.prose: The tempter reached for the psalm, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers from the Torah, as he does all three times in the wilderness. Moses had already named the place where Yashar'el (Israel) put Yahuah (the LORD) to the test, *as ye tempted him in Massah*, and the Son will not do it again. The commandment stands, and the one who gave it keeps it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Moses forbids putting Yahuah (the LORD) to the test as Yashar'el (Israel) did at Massah, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers the pinnacle with it.

cards.prose: The devil's way of reading the psalm would have Yahusha (Jesus) break a commandment to cash in a promise. John gives the plain test that catches it: knowing him shows in keeping *his commandments*, so any use of scripture that sets a commandment aside is not knowing him at all. Yahusha (Jesus) keeps the commandment, and the promise is left standing where the psalm put it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: John says we know him by keeping his commandments, which rules out any reading of scripture that sets them aside.

cards.prose: The devil quoted a true word and left out what stood beside it. Yahusha (Jesus) told the Sadducees they erred *not knowing the scriptures*, and that is the same fault seen from the other side. To know the scriptures is to know them whole, with the word that sits next to the one you quote, and on the pinnacle he sets the Torah beside the psalm.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) tells the Sadducees their error comes from not knowing the scriptures, the same fault the devil trades on at the pinnacle.

cards.prose: Peter says the unlearned and unstable *wrest* the scriptures to their own ruin, and the devil at the pinnacle is the first to do it, lifting a true word out of its place and bending it into a dare. The same twisting has been done to Paul's letters since, and the answer is the one given in the wilderness: read it beside what Yahuah (the LORD) already said.
cards.member_phrase: unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction
cards.member_sentence: Peter names the wresting of scripture that the devil begins at the pinnacle and that was later turned on Paul's letters.

cards.prose: Daniel is told of a prince standing behind the kingdom of Persia who held a messenger back *one and twenty days* until Michael came to help. Powers sit behind the kingdoms of the world, and that is what the devil is holding out on the mountain. He is offering what he administers, and Yahusha (Jesus) will not buy it.
cards.member_phrase: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia withstood me one and twenty days
cards.member_sentence: A prince stands behind the kingdom of Persia and resists the messenger, showing that powers sit behind the kingdoms of the world.

cards.prose: The messenger goes on to name the next one, the prince of Grecia, so the powers over the kingdoms come in a line as the kingdoms rise. The devil's sweep across all the kingdoms of the world takes in that whole line. What he shows is real, and the price of it is worship, which is the one thing Yahusha (Jesus) will not pay.
cards.member_phrase: and now will I return to fight with the prince of Persia: and when I am gone forth, lo, the prince of Grecia shall come.
cards.member_sentence: After the prince of Persia the prince of Grecia comes next, so the powers behind the kingdoms follow one another.

cards.prose: Paul says our struggle is not with flesh and blood but with *the rulers of the darkness of this world*. The devil on the mountain is one of those rulers showing his holdings. The people under the kingdoms are not the enemy, and Yahusha (Jesus) refuses the power behind them.
cards.member_phrase: against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world
cards.member_sentence: Paul names the principalities and rulers of this world's darkness as the real opponent, not the people under them.

cards.prose: John says the world as it stands *lieth in wickedness*, and that is the condition of the kingdoms the devil spreads out on the mountain. Those who belong to Elohim (God) know it. Yahusha (Jesus) will not take the world on the world's terms.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: John says the whole world lies in wickedness, which is the state of the kingdoms the devil holds out.

cards.prose:
The devil offers the kingdoms at once, for one act of worship. Daniel sees them given another way, to the one like the Son of Adam brought near the Ancient of days:

*And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom* (Daniel 7:14)

That is the Father's gift in the Father's time, and Yahusha (Jesus) waits for it rather than take it from the one with no right to give it.
cards.member_phrase: and they brought him near before him
cards.member_sentence: Daniel sees the kingdom given to the one like the Son of Adam in the Father's presence, not taken by a bow.

cards.prose: The kingdoms the devil held out do become the Messiah's (Christ's), but Revelation shows it happening at the sound of the seventh angel, with *great voices in heaven* announcing it. Yahusha (Jesus) refuses the short road by worship and receives the whole of it in the right hour.
cards.member_phrase: The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Messiah (Christ)
cards.member_sentence: The kingdoms of this world become the Messiah's (Christ's) at the seventh trumpet, on the Father's timing.

cards.prose: The serpent of the garden is the one now standing on the mountain, and the word spoken to him was that the woman's seed would *bruise* his head while he bruised the heel. The road to the kingdom runs through that heel, through the cross, and the offer on the mountain is a way around it. Yahusha (Jesus) will not skip what was spoken from the beginning.
cards.member_phrase: and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel
cards.member_sentence: The first word to the serpent says the seed of the woman will bruise his head, and the heel is bruised on the way.

cards.prose: The psalm gives its reason in the same breath: the one delivered is he who *hath set his love upon me*, and who *hath known my name*. The devil's dare asks for deliverance with no love in it, only proof. The one who loves the Father keeps his word, so he will not throw himself down to see whether he will be caught.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The promise of deliverance goes to the one who has set his love on Yahuah (the LORD) and known his name, not to a dare.

cards.prose: After the third refusal angels come and serve him, which is what the devil wanted to stage as a sign on the pinnacle. Hebrews says what angels are for, *ministering spirits* sent for the heirs, and here it simply happens, with no leap to force it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Angels are ministering spirits sent to serve the heirs, and here they come on their own once the testing is over.
cards.flag: The map thread for this card, matthew-4-the-temptation-in-the-wilderness, is not among the threads offered, so I placed it in the thread that holds verse 11.

cards.prose: Elijah lay worn out in the wilderness, and an angel touched him and fed him, and he went on *forty days and forty nights* (1 Kings 19:8) to Horeb. Yahusha (Jesus) has fasted the same forty days, and when the testing is done the same kind of help comes to him from the same hand.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: An angel touches Elijah in the wilderness and tells him to arise and eat, as angels serve Yahusha (Jesus) after his testing.
cards.flag: The map thread for this card, matthew-4-the-temptation-in-the-wilderness, is not among the threads offered, so I placed it in the thread that holds verse 11.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) takes up John's very words, with nothing changed. He does not start something new where John left off; he goes on with the same call, because the one who prepared the way and the one who came after are carrying one message.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: John the Immerser cries the same call to turn that Yahusha (Jesus) takes up in Galilee, one message passed on.

cards.prose: The kingdom he announces is the one Daniel told the king about, set up by the Elohim (God) of heaven in the days of those kings, and one that *shall never be destroyed*. It is not a new idea arriving with the gospel. It is the old promise being called near.
cards.member_phrase: shall the Elohim (God) of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed
cards.member_sentence: Daniel told the king the Elohim (God) of heaven would set up a kingdom that never ends, the kingdom Yahusha (Jesus) calls at hand.

cards.prose: Daniel saw *one like the Son of Adam* come to the Ancient of days to receive the kingdom, and that is whose kingdom Yahusha (Jesus) calls near. When he says it is at hand he speaks as the one Daniel saw, though the receiving of it waits on the Father's time.
cards.member_phrase: one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days
cards.member_sentence: Daniel sees the one like the Son of Adam brought to the Ancient of days, the king whose kingdom is at hand.

cards.prose:
Isaiah tells the fearful hearts to be strong, because their Elohim (God) is coming to save them. What that coming looks like is given next:

*Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* (Isaiah 35:5)

That is the work going on all through Galilee, every sickness healed among the people, and it is the sign Yahusha (Jesus) later points John to.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah promises that Elohim (God) will come and save, and the opened eyes and ears that follow are what Galilee sees.

cards.prose: Isaiah's anointed one is sent to *bind up the brokenhearted* and to open the prison to the bound, and Galilee is where that work is seen. The preaching and the healing in Matthew are one commission, with the Spirit of Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) resting on him.
cards.member_phrase: he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives
cards.member_sentence: The anointed one is sent to bind up the brokenhearted and free the captives, the commission Yahusha (Jesus) carries through Galilee.
